notes: Perfect claim overlap (C6, C90, C96, C97) regarding ecological interpretation. LLM finds the integration of data strongly supports that moths use GLV ratios to assess host quality and avoid competition/predation. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about ecological relevance, questioning experimental conditions (seed origin, species mixing, field damage comparisons).

High overlap (7/8 claims shared: C5, C55, C56, C57, C61, C91, C101). Both agree that field oviposition assays demonstrate Manduca preference for higher (Z)-3/(E)-2-ratios. Peer reviewers find the behavioral data valuable and do not challenge the validity of observations.

Strong overlap (7/10 claims shared: C46, C47, C48, C59, C98, C99, C100) on field experiments and moonlight effects. Both express uncertainty about the moonlight hypothesis. LLM cites inconsistent results and need for controlled experiments; peer reviewers criticize it as 'post-hoc' with insufficient replication (single replicate per moon phase) and suggest eliminating this aspect.

Good overlap (5/8 claims shared: C40, C41, C42, C43, C58) on laboratory volatile collection experiments. Both agree that OS-induced GLV ratio changes are well-demonstrated. Peer reviewers find the study 'interesting' and 'valuable' without challenging the volatile emission data validity.

Moderate overlap (5/10 claims shared: C4, C49, C50, C51, C60) on functional imaging and neural responses. Both support the isomer-specific neural response findings. Peer reviewers praise the 'combination of methodologies' and raise no concerns about the neurobiological data.

Partial overlap (3/10 claims shared: C52, C53, C54) on differential neural response characteristics. LLM R4 focuses on ROI response mechanisms while peer R3 covers broader neurobiological findings. Both support the neural data where claims overlap.

Minimal overlap (1 claim: C62). LLM R1 addresses laboratory volatile collection (SUPPORTED) while peer R2 focuses on field experiments and moonlight (UNCERTAIN). The single shared claim (C62) relates to light regime effects, where perspectives differ on evidence quality.

Minimal overlap (1 claim: C45). LLM R2 addresses field experiments with uncertainty about environmental factors, while peer R1 supports laboratory volatile collection data. The shared claim C45 relates to field GLV measurements where contexts differ.

Minimal overlap (1 claim: C3). Both support their respective findings, but LLM R1 focuses on volatile collection experiments while peer R3 covers neurobiological aspects. The shared claim C3 appears to be foundational context accepted by both.

Minimal overlap (1 claim: C90). LLM R6 addresses ecological interpretation while peer R4 focuses on behavioral observations. Both support their conclusions where they overlap on the general finding about moth perception and behavior.

Claims C108, C109, C110 regarding hexenyl acetate as primary detection mechanism and functional interpretations appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic interpretations.

Claims C92, C93, C94 regarding learning and experience in oviposition behavior appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these discussion points about behavioral mechanisms.

Claims C1, C2, C21, C22, C23, C24, C25, C36 regarding the 2010 Science paper foundation (isomerase mechanism, predator attraction) appear only in peer review results. Reviewers acknowledge this prior work as valid context but request better integration.
